meta.title: Clay County Public Safety Complex
meta.summary: A Public-Private Partnership (P3) to design, build, and finance a shared-use public safety and training campus (Sheriff, Fire Rescue, Emergency Management, 911/EOC, and a St. Johns River State College training component) on a 53+/- acre site near Green Cove Springs. RFP 25/26-085 is confirmed as a real, currently-active procurement. The official Bid Tabulation Form has now been directly reviewed: 4 companies submitted bids and 2 declined (No Bid); the document is a bid-opening record only and contains no evaluation scores or ranking. No land purchase, no total project cost, and no selected vendor have been confirmed from a primary document as of this research pass.
meta.disclaimer: This is an evidence-gathering project trail, not an accusation. Every figure below carries an explicit evidence status and a source. A reported number (like the $200M-$400M range circulating in the community) is not treated as fact unless traced to a primary county document.

rfp.title: Public Private Partnership (P3) to Design, Build and Finance a Public Safety Complex in Clay County
rfp.statusAsOf: Bid opening confirmed; evaluation/scoring outcome unverified (checked 2026-09-23)
rfp.statutoryAuthority: Florida Statute 255.065 (P3 authority for public entities to develop, operate, and finance projects serving a public purpose, including public safety facilities)
rfp.siteAcreage: 53+/- acres per the current official RFP text (Section 3.1/3.5), described as combined purchased property plus adjoining County property (a pond site). An earlier ~44-acre figure appears in initial research leads with no independently located source or date — it may reflect an earlier-stage proposal, a partial parcel count, or simply an imprecise informal figure; it is not treated as an established prior record here, only as context that the reported acreage has varied across informal accounts.
rfp.components: Clay County Public Safety Facilities, ~391,000 SF (Public Safety Administration/Sheriff + Fire Rescue offices, Emergency Operations Center/911 Dispatch, Logistics Warehouse, Fleet Maintenance, Paved Storage, Shared Training) plus a St. Johns River State College Training/Classroom component, ~152,000 SF across two buildings — combined ~543,000 SF. No jail or courthouse component is included in this RFP.
rfp.accessPoints: Rosemary Hill Rd, plus a second access point on the SE portion of the site along a not-yet-named planned road
rfp.neighboringDevelopment: Peters Creek Industrial/Business Park — the RFP text asks respondents to coordinate with this neighboring developer on shared utilities, stormwater, and transportation. (This is the RFP's own text describing an adjacent, separate development; it is not the same parcel as the "Peters Creek Business Park" name appearing in an unrelated geotechnical report reviewed elsewhere in this research pass — the two are not established as the same site.)
rfp.financingStructure: Progressive P3 model, phased: Phase 1 (Spatial Needs Assessment, Site Planning, Financing) -> Phase 2 (Building-by-Building Design) -> Phase 3 (Construction, only after County approval and execution of a Guaranteed Maximum Price for each facility). Financing is lease-leaseback or installment-based; the County retains land ownership and explicitly does not intend to bond this project. Some funding is designated in the County's Capital Improvement Plan budget.
rfp.evaluationProcess: An Evaluation Committee of no fewer than 9 members scores proposals individually with no cross-communication; scores are announced at a public Evaluation Meeting under Florida Statutes; the committee's ranking goes to the Board of County Commissioners for approval to enter negotiations (the Board may also request its own presentations). See evaluationCriteria below for the verified scoring rubric from the full RFP document.
rfp.estimatedBCCRecommendationDate: 2026-07-14 per the RFP's own published timeline — this date has passed as of this research pass with no confirmed public BCC action found yet (see openQuestions).

evaluationCriteria.notes: Read directly from the full RFP 25/26-085 document (Addendum Revision, pages 1-36 of 44; Evaluation Phases section), obtained via the user's own authorized OpenGov vendor account. This is the scoring rubric the Evaluation Committee is instructed to use — it is not itself a completed scoresheet, and no individual or aggregate scores from an actual evaluation have been located or reviewed.

bidders.entity: VanTrust Real Estate, LLC dba VTRE Development, LLC

bidOpening.documentId: Bid Tabulation Form, RFP 25/26-085, posted as Official Notice #2
bidOpening.notes: The official Bid Tabulation Form has been directly reviewed (obtained via the user's own authorized OpenGov vendor account — a document-access registration, not a government-vendor-qualification registration; see CLAUDE.md). It confirms 4 actual submitted bids and 2 declines ("No Bid"). Every submitted bid shows "Total: To Be Determined" — this is a generic bid-opening tabulation form; it contains NO evaluation scores, NO ranking, and NO recommendation of any kind. It predates the evaluation process entirely. Do not present the staffRanking table below as coming from, or confirmed by, this document.

respondents.entity: VanTrust Real Estate, LLC dba VTRE Development, LLC

staffRanking.notes: These four names and scores were supplied as a lead at the start of this research phase and remain UNVERIFIED. The names match the 4 actual bidders confirmed in the official Bid Tabulation Form (see bidOpening above), which is consistent with these being the real respondents — but the Bid Tabulation Form itself contains no scores or ranking of any kind, and no separate evaluation scoresheet, Evaluation Meeting minutes, or BCC award/ranking-acceptance record has been located or reviewed to confirm these specific point totals or this order. A Sept 8, 2026 BCC meeting's public-comment portion references a same-night board item involving "four proposals" with the "top two" separated by "only 2.3 points" — a citizen's paraphrase from a meeting transcript, not a reviewed board document, and its relationship (if any) to this specific 136.9/134.6/125.8/125.1 score set has not been established. Treat the four scores and this exact ranking as an unverified lead until the actual evaluation/selection record is obtained; do not present them as verified fact.

landAcquisition.site: Green Cove Springs, near the Peters Creek Industrial Park area and the First Coast Expressway, across from the Clay County Fairgrounds
landAcquisition.acreage: 53+/- acres per the RFP (see rfp.siteAcreage above)
landAcquisition.notes: As of a Nov 12, 2025 News4Jax report, the county had not yet secured land or funding — it was only "eyed." By the RFP's release (April 2026), the RFP text itself describes the 53-acre site as already assembled from "purchased property and adjoining County property (pond site)," implying at least a partial acquisition occurred between Nov 2025 and April 2026. No Clay County Property Appraiser parcel ID, purchase price, seller, or closing date has been located for that acquisition.

costRangeOrigin.status: LEAD / NEEDS VERIFICATION — a reported estimate, not an established cost
costRangeOrigin.finding: This is a reported estimate whose underlying primary-source cost document has not been located. No primary county document, presentation, video, RFP text, or news article found in this research pass repeats this range. The RFP text itself (Section 3.9 Pricing) explicitly defers total cost to Respondent proposals and per-facility negotiated Guaranteed Maximum Prices — it contains no project-wide cost estimate at all. This figure must not be presented as an established total project cost.

stateGrant.purpose: Planning and partial design of the Public Safety Complex
stateGrant.notes: Reported as coming from a Clay County government release; the county's own release page could not be independently pulled (site blocks automated access).

consolidationHistory.value: The complex would consolidate the Sheriff's Office, Fire Rescue, EMT, Emergency Management, and the 911/call center, currently scattered between the county courthouse and a building near the Fairgrounds on SR 16.
consolidationHistory.notes: No pre-2025 BCC agenda item originating the consolidation concept was located this pass.

relatedComponent_lawEnforcementAcademy.description: Preliminary, non-binding discussions between Clay County, St. Johns River State College, and SJR State President Joe Pickens about co-locating SJR State's law-enforcement/fire training academy at the complex site.

relatedComponent_publicSafetyBondProgram.description: A separate, already-existing $65 million Public Safety Bond Program funds several fire stations (including Fire Station 20, opened August 2025). This is DISTINCT from the Public Safety Complex P3 project and should not be conflated with it.
relatedComponent_publicSafetyBondProgram.notes: Surfaced incidentally; not independently verified this pass.

stateFundingComponents.note: Four FY2026-27 Florida Senate LFIR requests explicitly describe themselves as components of this same Public Safety Complex campus. See data/state-funding.json for full detail (all four are `publicSafetyComplexComponent: true`).

openQuestions: Who was actually selected (if anyone), and what were the actual evaluation scores/ranking — a BCC award agenda item, Evaluation Meeting minutes, or scoresheet would resolve this (the Bid Tabulation Form itself is confirmed NOT to contain this).
What is the actual total project cost, and does any primary document support the $200M-$400M community figure?
What parcel(s) make up the 53-acre site, when were they purchased, from whom, and for how much?
Did the BCC ever formally act on the Evaluation Committee's recommendation after the estimated 2026-07-14 date? Does the Sept 8, 2026 "item 24" public comment correspond to that action?
What is the relationship, if any, between the $65M Public Safety Bond Program and this P3 project?
